fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Dense Vegetation; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Long Driveway; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles and obstructions could significantly improve apparatus ingress and egress during an emergency response. Displaying a clearly visible address marker at the street frontage would assist responding units in locating the property quickly. Maintaining adequate turnaround space near the main building and detached structure would support apparatus positioning and staging. Trimming or managing dense vegetation along the driveway and access road could improve driver visibility and reduce travel time for responding units. Identifying and communicating any secondary access opportunities around the rear of the property to the local fire department in advance may assist with pre-incident planning.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Dense Shrub Cover; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Fuel Continuity; Heavy Brush; Scattered Shrubs; Wildland Interface; Single Access Route; Ladder Fuels
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing brush directly adjacent to the structure and creating greater separation between dense shrub cover and building surfaces could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce opportunities for fire to reach the structure. Managing ladder fuels beneath and around tree clusters would help interrupt vertical fuel continuity, reducing the potential for fire to move from ground-level vegetation into the tree canopy. Thinning and separating scattered shrubs and heavy brush within the immediate structure perimeter may further reduce fuel continuity across the property. Where mixed vegetation cover surrounds the structure on multiple sides, maintaining cleared or well-separated zones could improve conditions for suppression operations. Given the single access route serving the property, keeping that route clear of overhanging vegetation and encroaching brush on both sides would support firefighter access and improve evacuation movement. Continued attention to vegetation management within the structure's immediate surroundings would support long-term wildfire resilience at this wildland interface location.
